assignments.reason: This is the combined action of dancing and clapping — the very mechanism of the hands-and-feet system. Its essential nature is the physical expression of divine light through the body's extremities. The Torah opens (section א) by stating that through rikudim and hamcha'at kaf the sweetening of judgments is achieved. Package 1 already contains רקודים, המחאת כף, ידים, and רגלים separately; this combined form shares their essential nature as the active manifestation of the hands-and-feet dimension.

This concept describes the elevation of the feet through dancing — 'nasah libo et raglav' realized through the rikudin. Its essential nature is the feet-dimension being rectified and elevated, which is the core thematic domain of Package 1. The package already contains רגלים, רקודים, נשא לבו את רגליו, and הארת הרגלים — this concept shares their essential nature as the upward movement of the foot-dimension of holiness.

The sweetening of judgments is the stated purpose and culmination of the hands-and-feet system in this Torah. Section א opens: 'through rikudim and hamcha'at kaf, the sweetening of judgments is achieved.' Section ו explains: when the feet are elevated through dancing, pride/idolatry is nullified, charon-af departs, and chasadim flow — this IS the hamtakat hadinim. While it is an effect of the system, its essential nature in this Torah is inseparable from the hands-and-feet mechanism: it is what the hands-and-feet dimension produces and exists to accomplish. The concept represents the positive transformation that the foot-and-hand revelation achieves.

Drawing close to tzaddikim is essentially about the tzaddik-relationship — the human act of approaching the righteous. Section ה states: 'ha'eitza haye'utza levatel haga'avah... ha'ikar hu al yedei hitkarvut latzaddikim.' Its essential nature belongs to the tzaddik domain: the tzaddik is the ruach, and hitkarvut is the act of connecting to that ruach. Package 2 already contains צדיק, רוח, יוסף (the archetypal tzaddik), and the corrective/rebuking function. Drawing close to tzaddikim is the practical expression of entering the tzaddik's spiritual field.

The nullification of pride is a process-concept within the gaavah domain. Its essential nature is gaavah itself — the concept is defined by and inseparable from pride. Package 3 already contains גאוה, גאות, and the full pride-idolatry cluster. This node represents the event of that evil dimension being defeated. Though the nullification is a positive outcome, the concept's essential identity is 'pride' (being negated), placing it in the pride/idolatry domain. Polarity is evil because the concept refers to the evil substance (gaavah) that is being nullified.

The nullification of idolatry belongs to the avodah zarah domain by essential nature. The Torah equates gaavah with avodah zarah (section ה: 'haga'avah shehi ha'avodah zarah'), and this concept represents the destruction of that evil. Package 3 already contains עבודה זרה, המן (who made himself an idol), and the full evil cluster. This node represents the event of idolatry's defeat. Polarity is evil because the concept refers to the evil substance (avodah zarah) being nullified.

The nullification of heresies belongs to the evil domain. Kefirot (heresies/denials of God) are functionally equivalent to minut (heresy), which is already in Package 3. The Torah states (section ו): 'venitbatel ha'avodah zarah, hainu hakefirot' — kefirot ARE avodah zarah. Package 3 already contains מינות and נטיו רגלי (the fallen feet = heresy). This concept shares their essential nature as the domain of denial/heresy. Polarity is evil because it refers to the evil substance (kefirot) being nullified.
